meta.epistemic_status: derived from curated variant classes; no efficiency or safety parameters are used
caveats: Every gene here is allelically heterogeneous to some degree, so assigning one dominant variant class per condition is an approximation. Conditions where that matters most are flagged as heterogeneous.

Gate 2 asks only whether a platform could make the molecular change in principle. It is not a claim that the change can be made in an embryo, efficiently, or safely — those are gates 3 and 4, and neither is established.
No editing efficiency, mosaicism or off-target figures are used anywhere in this module; sourcing them is listed in DATA_NEEDED.md.
The S1 population itself carries the credible interval reported on the residual view; the split below uses median values only.

gene_addition.label: Gene addition
gene_addition.mechanism: Deliver a functional copy of the gene (AAV, lentiviral) without changing the endogenous sequence.
gene_addition.examples: Zolgensma (AAV9, SMA); Lenmeldy (lentiviral, MLD); Luxturna (AAV, RPE65)
gene_addition.germline_status: not applicable — an added copy is not a heritable correction of the causal variant

nuclease.label: Nuclease editing (CRISPR-Cas9)
nuclease.mechanism: Cut the DNA and let the cell repair it. Reliable for disrupting a sequence; precise correction requires a repair template and is inefficient.
nuclease.examples: Casgevy — note this DISRUPTS a BCL11A enhancer to raise fetal haemoglobin; it does not correct the sickle variant
nuclease.germline_status: double-strand breaks in embryos are associated with mosaicism, large on-target deletions and chromosome loss

base_editor.label: Base editing
base_editor.mechanism: Chemically convert one base pair to another without cutting both strands. Performs transitions only: C·G→T·A and A·T→G·C.
base_editor.examples: Cytosine and adenine base editors (Komor 2016; Gaudelli 2017)

prime_editor.label: Prime editing
prime_editor.mechanism: Write a new sequence from an attached template. In principle handles all twelve substitutions plus small insertions and deletions.

epigenetic.label: Epigenetic editing
epigenetic.mechanism: Change gene expression without altering sequence. Not a correction, and heritability across generations is not established.

transition_snv.label: Point mutation (transition)
transition_snv.detail: A single base swapped within the purines or within the pyrimidines (C↔T, A↔G). The class base editors were built for.

transversion_snv.label: Point mutation (transversion)
transversion_snv.detail: A single base swapped between a purine and a pyrimidine (e.g. A→T). Standard base editors cannot make this change.

small_indel.label: Small insertion or deletion
small_indel.detail: A few bases added or lost. Requires writing sequence back, not swapping a base.

large_deletion.label: Large deletion or duplication
large_deletion.detail: Whole exons or genes lost or duplicated. There is no established route to restore the missing sequence.

repeat_expansion.label: Repeat expansion
repeat_expansion.detail: A short sequence repeated far too many times. Contracting a repeat is not an established capability.

chromosomal_structural.label: Chromosomal rearrangement
chromosomal_structural.detail: Whole segments of chromosomes joined or reordered. Not a sequence variant at all — there is nothing to rewrite, the chromosomes themselves are rearranged.

gates.label: Selection cannot help
gates.question: Is there any embryo this couple could select that would be unaffected?
gates.detail: The S1 population: couples for whom no unaffected embryo exists. This is the only gate where editing has a distinctive claim in the first place.

gates.label: The variant has a correction route
gates.question: Does any platform exist that could make this molecular change at all?
gates.detail: Determined by the class of variant. Restoring a large deletion or contracting a repeat expansion is not something any current platform can do.

gates.label: The platform works in an embryo
gates.question: Has that platform been shown to work safely in a human embryo?
gates.detail: Editing a single-cell embryo is not the same problem as editing cells in a dish. Nuclease approaches carry documented mosaicism and chromosome-loss risks; base and prime editing have no established embryo application.

gates.label: It is safe enough to use
gates.question: Are off-target and mosaicism risks low enough to justify use?
gates.detail: Requires efficiency and safety data this project has not sourced. Left explicitly unquantified rather than assigned a placeholder.

conditions.tractability_label: Only prime editing could make the change
conditions.explanation: 35delG, a single-base deletion, predominates in European-ancestry populations; 235delC predominates in East Asia. Both are deletions rather than substitutions. This condition is also contested as a target and is excluded from the headline.

conditions.tractability_label: Only prime editing could make the change
conditions.explanation: HbS is a single substitution, GAG→GTG (Glu6Val) — an A·T→T·A transversion. It is the textbook point mutation, yet standard base editors perform transitions, so they cannot revert it. Casgevy does not correct it either: it disrupts a BCL11A enhancer to raise fetal haemoglobin, which is mitigation rather than correction.
conditions.citation: Ingram 1957 (HbS substitution); Frangoul et al. 2021 (exagamglogene, BCL11A)
conditions.reported_alleles_note: 415 pathogenic HBB alleles are reported, but they cover every disorder in the gene rather than this one, so the count does not describe it.

conditions.tractability_label: No current platform can restore the sequence
conditions.explanation: Carriers whose chromosome rearrangement leaves no viable euploid embryo. This is the clearest case of a condition outside editing's reach: there is no variant to correct, because whole chromosome segments are in the wrong place. It is nonetheless one of the largest contributors to the population where selection fails, which is why the distinction matters.
conditions.citation: Scriven et al., translocation PGT outcomes; Zhang et al., carrier segregation

conditions.tractability_label: A mature platform could make the change
conditions.explanation: Several hundred HBB alleles are known. Many common ones are point mutations, a substantial share of them transitions (e.g. IVS-I-110 G>A), but others are small indels. The share that is base-editable is population-specific and is approximated here rather than measured.

conditions.tractability_label: Only prime editing could make the change
conditions.explanation: F508del, a three-base deletion, is the most common CFTR allele worldwide. Losing bases means sequence has to be written back, which is prime-editing territory. Other alleles are point mutations, so a minority would be base-editable.

conditions.tractability_label: No current platform can restore the sequence
conditions.explanation: Around 95% of cases are homozygous loss of SMN1 exon 7. There is no established way to restore a deleted gene, which is exactly why the approved therapies are gene ADDITION (Zolgensma) and splice modulation of the SMN2 backup copy (nusinersen) rather than correction. A clear case where addition works and editing does not.
conditions.citation: Lefebvre et al. 1995 (SMN1); Mendell et al. 2017 (onasemnogene)

conditions.tractability_label: No current platform can restore the sequence
conditions.explanation: An expanded CAG repeat in HTT. Contracting a repeat is not an established capability for any platform, which is why therapeutic work targets lowering huntingtin expression rather than correcting the allele.

conditions.tractability_label: Only prime editing could make the change
conditions.explanation: The most common Ashkenazi founder allele, 1278insTATC, is a four-base insertion; a splice-site variant and a point mutation make up most of the remainder. Founder-population structure means the dominant class is ancestry-dependent.

base_editable.label: A mature platform could make the change

prime_only.label: Only prime editing could make the change

no_current_route.label: No current platform can restore the sequence

base_editable_caveat.why: The whole base-editable bucket is beta-thalassaemia, which is allelically heterogeneous. Its commonest alleles span three variant classes, so some of this population needs prime editing rather than base editing.

common_alleles.name: CD41/42
common_alleles.where: Southeast Asia / China — a four-base deletion

base_editable_caveat.what_is_missing: How often each allele occurs among affected births. The spectrum is strongly population-specific, so weighting it needs a population-weighted allele-frequency source.
base_editable_caveat.citation: Kountouris et al., IthaGenes; regional beta-thalassaemia spectrum literature (see REVIEW_TRACKER B3)
